requirements.title: Scope registry and the scope check
requirements.rationale: Every package's routes rely on one registry and one check, so a PAT is held to the same rule everywhere.

criteria.action: treat exactly these 32 case-sensitive names as registered scopes and every other string as unregistered: users:read, users:write, orgs:read, keys:read, keys:manage, tokens:read, tokens:write, tokens:manage, workspaces:read, workspaces:write, git:read, git:write, changes:read, changes:write, changes:approve, checks:write, patches:read, patches:write, rebuilds:read, rebuilds:write, secrets:read, secrets:write, vars:read, vars:write, forge:read, forge:write, sandboxes:read, sandboxes:write, audit:read, audit:write, sessions:read, sessions:write
criteria.contract: the scope validator returns true for each of the 32 names and false for any other string

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/scope_test.go: for each of the 32 names assert IsRegisteredScope(name); assert len(RegisteredScopes()) == 32; table of refused strings {'', 'git', 'git:', ':read', 'git:admin', 'GIT:READ', 'checks:read', 'orgs:write', 'keys:write', 'tokens:approve', ' git:read'}: assert !IsRegisteredScope(s)

criteria.condition: a request authenticated with a PAT reaches the scope check of a route that declares a needed scope
criteria.action: pass the request to the next check when the PAT holds the needed scope itself, or the route needs R:read and the PAT holds R:write, or the route needs keys:read and the PAT holds keys:manage, or the route needs tokens:read and the PAT holds tokens:write or tokens:manage, or the route needs tokens:write and the PAT holds tokens:manage
criteria.contract: the next check or the handler runs; the scope check writes no response

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/scope_test.go, a table over (held scopes, needed scope, want): {[git:read], git:read, pass}, {[git:write], git:read, pass}, {[git:read], git:write, refuse}, {[users:write], users:read, pass}, {[keys:manage], keys:read, pass}, {[keys:read], keys:manage, refuse}, {[tokens:manage], tokens:write, pass}, {[tokens:manage], tokens:read, pass}, {[tokens:write], tokens:read, pass}, {[tokens:write], tokens:manage, refuse}, {[tokens:read], tokens:write, refuse}, {[changes:write], changes:approve, refuse}, {[changes:approve], changes:read, refuse}, {[changes:approve], changes:write, refuse}, {[changes:approve], changes:approve, pass}, {[checks:write], checks:write, pass}, {[changes:write], checks:write, refuse}, {[git:write], changes:read, refuse}, {[], git:read, refuse}: assert Satisfies(held, needed) == want; then through the server pipeline with a stub handler: a PAT caller with [git:write] on a route declaring git:read reaches the handler

criteria.condition: a request authenticated with a PAT reaches the scope check and the PAT holds neither the needed scope nor a scope that implies it
criteria.action: refuse the request before the workspace access check, the admin check, request validation and the handler run
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with the error envelope, error_type insufficient_scope, and a message that names the needed scope; the same answer whether or not the addressed resource exists; the handler is not called

setup: the server pipeline of internal/server with the scope check installed at its position and a stub authenticator that reports a PAT caller
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/scope_test.go: register a route declaring git:write whose handler records calls and whose later check would answer 404; send a request as a PAT caller holding [git:read]; assert status == 403; assert body.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert body.error.code == 403; assert 'git:write' in body.error.message; assert handler calls == 0 and the later check was not called

criteria.action: for any request authenticated with the admin token or an API key, pass the scope check of every route whatever scope the route declares, and pass any request on a route that declares no scope
criteria.contract: the next check or the handler runs

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/scope_test.go, a table over callers {admin token, API key of a role-user user, API key of a role-admin user} and needed scopes {git:write, changes:approve, checks:write, tokens:manage}: the stub handler is reached; and a PAT caller with [git:read] on a route that declares no scope reaches the handler

criteria.action: for any PAT that does not hold changes:approve, refuse a check for changes:approve, and likewise for checks:write; and let changes:approve and checks:write satisfy no check other than the one for themselves

requirements.title: API keys: list, refresh and revoke
requirements.rationale: A person must be able to see their keys, rotate a secret without a new login and cut off a key that leaked.

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding keys:read or keys:manage) sends GET /user/keys
criteria.action: answer with every API key of the caller in any state (live, revoked, expired), newest first by created_at then key_id descending, each as a Key object with the members key_id, user_id, expires_at, revoked_at and created_at and no secret
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: Key[], next_cursor}; expires_at and revoked_at are null when unset

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has three keys created at different instants: one live, one revoked, one expired; bob has one key
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go: r = GET /api/v1/user/keys as alice's live key; assert r.status == 200; assert ids(r.items) == [newest..oldest] and all three states are present; assert no item has a member named key or secret; assert bob's key is absent; as alice's PAT with [keys:read] and with [keys:manage]: 200; as alice's PAT with [git:read]: 403 insufficient_scope

criteria.condition: an API key sends POST /user/keys/:key_id/refresh naming a live key of its own user
criteria.action: replace the key's secret with a new random one, keep key_id, set expires_at to the present instant plus the key's expires_days (null when expires_days is 0), and stop accepting the old secret at once
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {key: 'parley_<key_id>_<new secret>', key_id, expires_at}; a later request with the old secret gets HTTP 401 and one with the new key authenticates

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live key K was created with expires_days 30
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go: advance the clock 10 days; r = POST /api/v1/user/keys/<K>/refresh as old key value; assert r.status == 200; assert r.key matches ^parley_<K>_[0-9A-Za-z]{32}$ and r.key != old value; assert r.key_id == K; assert r.expires_at == clock.now + 30 days; assert GET /user/keys with the old value -> 401; with r.key -> 200 and the listed key K has the new expires_at; table row for a key with expires_days 0: r.expires_at == null

criteria.condition: POST /user/keys/:key_id/refresh is sent with a PAT or with the admin token
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the key unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden; the admin token gets the message "this route needs a user" of package 04; the key's secret and expires_at are unchanged

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live key K
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go, a table over callers {alice's PAT holding keys:manage, the admin token}: r = POST /api/v1/user/keys/<K>/refresh; assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'forbidden'; assert alice's key value still authenticates

criteria.condition: an API key sends POST /user/keys/:key_id/refresh naming a key of its own user that is revoked or expired
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the key unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type conflict; the key record is unchanged

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has a second live key, a revoked key and an expired key
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go, a table over target keys {revoked, expired}: r = POST /api/v1/user/keys/<target>/refresh as alice's other live key; assert r.status == 409; assert r.error.error_type == 'conflict'; assert the stored record of the target is unchanged

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding keys:manage) sends DELETE /user/keys/:key_id naming a key of its own user that is not revoked
criteria.action: set the key's revoked_at to the present instant and keep the record, also when the key is expired and also when the key is the one that authenticated the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Key, revoked_at set; the key no longer authenticates

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has live keys K1 and K3 and an expired key K2
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go, a table over (caller, target): {live key K1, K1 itself}, {live key K1, expired key K2}, {alice's PAT with [keys:manage], live key K3}: r = DELETE /api/v1/user/keys/<target>; assert r.status == 200; assert r.key_id == target and r.revoked_at == clock.now; for the self-revoke row assert a following GET /user/keys with K1 -> 401; row {alice's PAT with [keys:read], K3}: 403 insufficient_scope and K3 not revoked

criteria.condition: DELETE /user/keys/:key_id names a key of the caller's user that is already revoked
criteria.action: change nothing and answer with the key as stored
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Key; revoked_at keeps its earlier value

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has live keys K1 (the caller) and K2
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go: first = DELETE /api/v1/user/keys/<K2>; advance the clock one hour; second = DELETE again; assert second.status == 200; assert second.revoked_at == first.revoked_at

criteria.condition: POST /user/keys/:key_id/refresh or DELETE /user/keys/:key_id names a key_id that does not exist or belongs to another user
criteria.action: refuse the request with the same answer in both cases and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; the response for another user's key equals the response for a missing key; no key is changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
user bob with a live API key
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/key_routes_test.go, a table over routes {POST /user/keys/:id/refresh, DELETE /user/keys/:id} and ids {'zzzzzzzz' (no such key), bob's live key id}: as alice's live key assert r.status == 404; assert r.error.error_type == 'not_found'; assert the body for bob's key id equals the body for the missing id on the same route; assert bob's key still authenticates

requirements.title: Creating a PAT
requirements.rationale: Automation gets a credential of its own with only the scopes it needs, and its value is shown exactly once.

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:manage) sends POST /user/tokens with a valid body
criteria.action: create a PAT owned by the caller's user with a new token_id of 8 and a secret of 32 characters from [a-z0-9], the name given, the permissions given with duplicates dropped and the order kept, paths as given or null, workspace null, and store only a hash of the secret
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the Token object plus token: 'parley_pat_<token_id>_<secret>'; the returned value authenticates as the new PAT

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens {name:'ci', permissions:['git:write','changes:write','git:write']} as alice's API key; assert r.status == 201; assert r.token matches ^parley_pat_[a-z0-9]{8}_[a-z0-9]{32}$ and contains r.token_id; assert r.permissions == ['git:write','changes:write']; assert r.paths == null and r.workspace == null and r.revoked_at == null; assert r.user_id == alice.id; assert r.created_at == clock.now; assert the store holds no column equal to the secret; assert GET /api/v1/user with r.token is authenticated (not 401); row with name of 255 characters: 201

criteria.condition: POST /user/tokens creates a PAT
criteria.action: set expires_at to the creation instant plus expires times 24 hours for 30, 60 and 90, to null for 0, and use 90 when expires is absent
criteria.contract: the Token's expires_at is the stated instant or null; once that instant has passed the token is expired and no longer authenticates

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over expires {absent -> now+90d, 0 -> null, 30 -> now+30d, 60 -> now+60d, 90 -> now+90d}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 201; assert r.expires_at == want, formatted as RFC 3339 UTC with whole seconds; then for the 30 row: at clock = expires_at - 1s the token authenticates, at clock = expires_at + 1s a request with it gets 401

criteria.condition: the body of POST /user/tokens has a name that is missing, not a string, empty or longer than 255 characters, or permissions that is missing, not an array, empty or holds a string that is not a registered scope, or an expires that is not one of the integers 0, 30, 60 and 90
criteria.action: refuse the request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the caller's token list is unchanged

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table of bodies: {no name}, {name:''}, {name of 256 characters}, {name: 5}, {no permissions}, {permissions: []}, {permissions: 'git:read'}, {permissions: ['git:read','git:admin']}, {permissions: ['GIT:READ']}, {expires: 45}, {expires: -1}, {expires: '30'}, {expires: 30.5}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens as alice's API key; assert r.status == 400; assert r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; after all rows assert GET /user/tokens returns items == []

criteria.condition: POST /user/tokens is sent with a PAT that does not hold tokens:manage
criteria.action: refuse the request before validating the body and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, also when the body is invalid; no token is created

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has PATs with the listed scopes
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over the caller PAT's scopes {[tokens:write], [tokens:read], [git:write]} and bodies {valid, {}}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert alice's token count is unchanged

criteria.condition: any route under /user/keys or /user/tokens is called with the admin token
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type forbidden and the message "this route needs a user", the one answer package 04 gives the admin token on a route that needs a user; no key or token is created or changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
the hub's admin token
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (method, path): {GET /user/keys}, {POST /user/keys/x/refresh}, {DELETE /user/keys/x}, {POST /user/tokens}, {GET /user/tokens}, {GET /user/tokens/x}, {DELETE /user/tokens/x}, {PUT, PATCH, DELETE /user/tokens/x/permissions}: send with the admin token (and a valid body where one is taken); assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'forbidden'

criteria.condition: POST /user/tokens is repeated within 24 hours by the same caller with the same Idempotency-Key and the same body as a request that created a PAT
criteria.action: create nothing and answer with the body of the first response without its token member
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token object and no token member; exactly one PAT exists

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: first = POST /api/v1/user/tokens with header Idempotency-Key: k1 and body B; second = the same request again; assert first.status == 201 and second.status == 200; assert second.token_id == first.token_id; assert 'token' not in second; assert GET /user/tokens returns one item

criteria.action: for any PAT, include its value in the response that created it and in no other response
criteria.contract: Token objects returned by list, read, permission-change, revoke and admin routes carry no token member

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: create a PAT, then collect the bodies of GET /user/tokens, GET /user/tokens/<id>, PUT /user/tokens/<id>/permissions, DELETE /user/tokens/<id> and, with an admin key, GET /users/alice/tokens and DELETE /users/alice/tokens/<id>; assert no body has a member named token and no body contains the secret text

requirements.title: The subset rule
requirements.rationale: A token that could mint a stronger token would make every scope limit meaningless.

criteria.condition: a PAT holding tokens:manage sends POST /user/tokens, and it holds every requested permission exactly, and it either has no paths or every requested glob is covered by one of its own globs
criteria.action: create the PAT as an API key caller's request would
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 with the Token and its value

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has the caller PATs of the table
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (caller PAT, request): {[tokens:manage, git:read] no paths, permissions [git:read]}, {same, permissions [git:read, tokens:manage]}, {same, permissions [git:read] paths ['docs/**']}, {[tokens:manage, git:write] paths ['src/**'], permissions [git:write] paths ['src/api/*.go']}, {same, permissions [git:write] paths ['src/**']}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 201; assert r.permissions and r.paths equal the request's

criteria.condition: a PAT holding tokens:manage sends POST /user/tokens with a valid body that requests a permission the PAT does not itself hold, counting no implication
criteria.action: refuse the request, name the first requested permission in request order that the caller does not hold, and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope and a message containing the first offending permission; no token is created

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has the caller PATs of the table
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (caller scopes, requested, named): {[tokens:manage, git:write], [git:read], 'git:read'}, {[tokens:manage, git:read], [git:read, changes:write, vars:read], 'changes:write'}, {[tokens:manage], [tokens:write], 'tokens:write'}, {[tokens:manage, changes:write], [changes:approve], 'changes:approve'}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert named in r.error.message; assert alice's token count is unchanged

criteria.condition: a PAT that has paths and holds tokens:manage sends POST /user/tokens with a valid body whose paths is absent or null, or holds a glob that none of the caller's globs covers
criteria.action: refuse the request, name the first requested glob in request order that none of the caller's globs covers (or say that paths is required when none was requested), and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope and a message containing the first offending glob; no token is created

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has the caller PAT
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, with a caller PAT [tokens:manage, git:write] paths ['src/**', 'docs/*'], a table over requested paths and the text expected in the message: {absent, 'paths'}, {null, 'paths'}, {['src/a.go', 'lib/**'], 'lib/**'}, {['docs/**'], 'docs/**'}, {['**'], '**'}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens {permissions:['git:write'], paths}; assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert text in r.error.message; assert alice's token count is unchanged

criteria.action: for any POST /user/tokens sent with an API key, apply no subset rule: accept every set of registered scopes and every valid paths
criteria.contract: HTTP 201 for any valid body

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: as alice's API key (role user) POST /api/v1/user/tokens with all 32 registered scopes and paths ['**']; assert r.status == 201; assert len(r.permissions) == 32

criteria.condition: a PAT holding tokens:manage sends POST /user/tokens with a body that fails validation and also requests a permission or glob the PAT does not hold
criteria.action: answer the validation failure, not the subset rule
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; no token is created

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: as a PAT [tokens:manage, git:read], table of bodies {permissions ['git:admin']}, {permissions ['git:read'], paths []}, {permissions ['git:write'], expires 45}: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 400; assert r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'

requirements.title: Path globs: the paths field, matching and covering
requirements.rationale: One definition of what a glob matches and what it covers keeps minting and write enforcement in agreement.

criteria.condition: POST /user/tokens creates a PAT from a body whose paths is an array of 1 to 50 globs, each a string of 1 to 255 characters that does not start with /
criteria.action: store the globs in the order given, without removing duplicates, and return them as paths in the creation response and in every later Token object of that token
criteria.contract: HTTP 201; paths in the response equals the array sent; a body without paths or with paths null yields paths null

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens {name:'d', permissions:['users:read'], paths:['docs/**','src/*.go','docs/**']} as alice's API key; assert r.status == 201 (a token without any write scope is accepted); assert r.paths == ['docs/**','src/*.go','docs/**']; assert GET /user/tokens/<id>.paths and the item in GET /user/tokens carry the same list; rows: a list of exactly 50 globs -> 201; a glob of exactly 255 characters -> 201; paths: null -> 201 with paths null

criteria.condition: the body of POST /user/tokens has a paths that is an empty array, not an array, an array of more than 50 entries, or holds an entry that is not a string, is empty, is longer than 255 characters or starts with /
criteria.action: refuse the request and create nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; no token is created

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/pathglob_test.go, a table over paths values: [], a list of 51 globs, [''], [a string of 256 characters], ['/src/**'], ['docs/**', 7], 'docs/**', {}: assert ValidatePaths(v) returns an error; and in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go for the rows [], 51 globs and ['/src/**']: r = POST /api/v1/user/tokens; assert r.status == 400; assert r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert alice's token count is unchanged

criteria.action: for any glob and any repository file path, report a match exactly when the whole path matches the glob read left to right with * as any run (also empty) of characters other than /, ** as any run (also empty) of characters including /, and every other character as itself, compared case-sensitively
criteria.contract: the matcher returns true or false; for a token without paths every path is allowed

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/pathglob_test.go, a table over (glob, path, want): {docs/**, docs/a.md, true}, {docs/**, docs/api/b.md, true}, {docs/**, docs, false}, {docs/**, xdocs/a.md, false}, {src/*.go, src/main.go, true}, {src/*.go, src/x/y.go, false}, {src/*.go, src/.go, true}, {src/*.go, src/main.go.bak, false}, {**, any/deep/file, true}, {*, a/b, false}, {*, a, true}, {**/*.md, docs/a.md, true}, {**/*.md, a.md, false}, {README.md, README.md, true}, {README.md, readme.md, false}, {a?c, abc, false}, {a?c, a?c, true}, {a[b]c, a[b]c, true}, {a[b]c, abc, false}, {src/**/test/*, src/a/b/test/x, true}: assert MatchPath(glob, path) == want; and MatchAny(['docs/**','src/*.go'], 'src/main.go') == true; MatchAny(same, 'lib/x') == false; MatchAny(nil, 'lib/x') == true (no paths means unrestricted)

criteria.action: for any two globs C and G, report that C covers G exactly when C equals G, or C used as a pattern matches the text of G taken literally where a * of C matches a run that has no / and does not contain the sequence ** and a ** of C matches any run
criteria.contract: the cover test returns true or false and never returns true for a requested glob that matches a path the covering glob does not match

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/pathglob_test.go, a table over (C, G, want): {src/**, src/api/*.go, true}, {src/**, src/**, true}, {src/*, src/**, false}, {src/**, docs/**, false}, {src/*, src/*, true}, {src/*, src/*.go, true}, {src/*, src/a**, false}, {src/*, src/a/b, false}, {**, anything/**, true}, {**, *, true}, {*, **, false}, {src/*.go, src/main.go, true}, {src/*.go, src/**, false}, {docs/*, docs/**, false}, {a/**/c, a/b/**/c, true}: assert Covers(C, G) == want; and CoveredByAny(['src/**','docs/*'], 'docs/a.md') == true; CoveredByAny(same, 'lib/**') == false

criteria.action: for any pair of globs for which the cover test answers true and any file path the requested glob matches, have the covering glob match that path too
criteria.contract: no counter-example exists over the generated domain

check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/pathglob_test.go: generate globs from the alphabet {a, b, /, *, **, .} up to 6 tokens and paths from {a, b, /, .} up to 8 characters (exhaustive or seeded random, at least 20000 triples); for each (C, G, p) with Covers(C, G) and MatchPath(G, p): assert MatchPath(C, p)

requirements.title: Reading and revoking PATs
requirements.rationale: A user must be able to see every token issued in their name and cut one off at once.

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:read, tokens:write or tokens:manage) sends GET /user/tokens
criteria.action: answer with every PAT of the caller's user in any state, tokens with a workspace binding included, newest first by created_at then token_id descending
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: Token[], next_cursor}; paths, workspace, expires_at and revoked_at are null when unset

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has four PATs created at different instants: live, revoked, expired, and one stored with workspace 'my-ws'; bob has one PAT
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = GET /api/v1/user/tokens as alice's API key; assert r.status == 200; assert ids(r.items) are in newest-first order and number 4; assert the bound item has workspace == 'my-ws'; assert bob's token is absent; with limit=2 follow next_cursor and assert the two pages hold the 4 ids once each; as alice's PATs with [tokens:read], [tokens:write] and [tokens:manage]: 200

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:read, tokens:write or tokens:manage) sends GET /user/tokens/:token_id naming a PAT of its own user
criteria.action: answer with that token's Token object
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token object

alice has a live, a revoked and an expired PAT
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = GET /api/v1/user/tokens/<id> as alice's API key for each of alice's live, revoked and expired tokens; assert r.status == 200; assert r.token_id == id and r.name, r.permissions, r.paths, r.expires_at, r.revoked_at, r.created_at equal the stored values

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:manage) sends DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id naming a PAT of its own user that is not revoked
criteria.action: set the token's revoked_at to the present instant and keep the record, also when the token is expired and also when the token is the one that authenticated the request
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token, revoked_at set; the token no longer authenticates

alice has live PATs T1 and T3 and an expired PAT T2
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (caller, target): {alice's API key, live T1}, {alice's API key, expired T2}, {PAT T3 holding tokens:manage, T3 itself}: r = DELETE /api/v1/user/tokens/<target>; assert r.status == 200; assert r.revoked_at == clock.now; assert r.permissions is unchanged; for T1 and T3 assert a following GET /api/v1/user with the token value -> 401

criteria.condition: DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id names a PAT of the caller's user that is already revoked
criteria.action: change nothing and answer with the token as stored
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token; revoked_at keeps its earlier value

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has a live PAT T1

criteria.condition: a route under /user/tokens/:token_id names a token_id that does not exist or belongs to another user
criteria.action: refuse the request with the same answer in both cases and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; the response for another user's token equals the response for a missing one; no token is changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
user bob with a live PAT [git:write]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over routes {GET /user/tokens/:id, DELETE /user/tokens/:id, PUT /user/tokens/:id/permissions, PATCH /user/tokens/:id/permissions, DELETE /user/tokens/:id/permissions} and ids {'zzzzzzzz', bob's token id}: as alice's API key with body {permissions:['git:read']} where one is taken; assert r.status == 404; assert r.error.error_type == 'not_found'; assert the body for bob's id equals the body for the missing id; assert bob's token is unchanged

criteria.condition: a PAT calls GET /user/tokens or GET /user/tokens/:token_id without tokens:read, tokens:write or tokens:manage, or DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id without tokens:manage, or a permissions route without tokens:write or tokens:manage
criteria.action: refuse the request before looking the token up
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope, the same for an existing and a missing token_id; nothing is changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has PATs with the listed scopes
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (route, caller PAT scopes): {GET /user/tokens, [git:read]}, {GET /user/tokens/:id, [keys:manage]}, {DELETE /user/tokens/:id, [tokens:write]}, {DELETE /user/tokens/:id, [tokens:read]}, {PUT /user/tokens/:id/permissions, [tokens:read]}, {PATCH /user/tokens/:id/permissions, [tokens:read]}, {DELETE /user/tokens/:id/permissions, [git:write]}, each with :id an existing token of alice and with :id 'zzzzzzzz': assert r.status == 403; assert r.error.error_type == 'insufficient_scope'; assert the existing token is unchanged

criteria.condition: a hub-internal caller asks for the revocation by id of one token, giving a transaction of its own and a token_id
criteria.action: set revoked_at of that token to now through the given transaction when it is null, without committing, without an ownership check and without writing an event, and leave an already revoked token unchanged
criteria.contract: after the caller commits, the token has revoked_at set to the clock's time, every other member is unchanged, and a request with the token is answered HTTP 401; after the caller rolls back, the token is as before and still authenticates; an expired token is revoked the same way; an already revoked token keeps its revoked_at and no error is returned; a token_id that does not exist returns a not-found error and writes nothing; no other token is changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has live PATs T1 and T2, a PAT T3 that has expired and a PAT T4 revoked one hour ago; user bob has a live PAT B1
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_ops_test.go: tx = store.Begin(); err = identity.RevokeTokenByID(tx, T1.id); assert err == nil; tx.Rollback(); assert T1 stored unchanged and GET /api/v1/user/tokens with T1 is 200; then a table over ids {T1, T3, B1}: tx = store.Begin(); assert identity.RevokeTokenByID(tx, id) == nil; tx.Commit(); assert stored revoked_at == clock.now and every other member is as before; assert a request with T1's value is 401; assert T2 is unchanged; tx = store.Begin(); assert identity.RevokeTokenByID(tx, T4.id) == nil; tx.Commit(); assert T4.revoked_at is the earlier value; err = identity.RevokeTokenByID(tx2, 'zzzzzzzz'); assert errors.Is(err, the not-found error of internal/identity); assert no row changed and no event was written

criteria.condition: a hub-internal caller asks for the expiry update of one token by id, giving a transaction of its own, a token_id and an instant
criteria.action: set expires_at of that token to the instant, in whole seconds, through the given transaction, without committing, without an ownership check and without writing an event, and change no other member
criteria.contract: after the caller commits, the token's expires_at equals the instant and every other member, revoked_at included, is unchanged; the token authenticates while the clock is before the instant and is answered HTTP 401 from the instant on, by the expiry predicate of package 04; after the caller rolls back, expires_at is as before; a token_id that does not exist returns a not-found error and writes nothing; no other token is changed

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice has a live PAT T1 that expires in 1 hour, a live PAT T2 and a PAT T4 revoked one hour ago
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_ops_test.go: later = clock.now + 6h; tx = store.Begin(); assert identity.SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, T1.id, later) == nil; tx.Rollback(); assert T1.expires_at is the earlier value; tx = store.Begin(); assert identity.SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, T1.id, later) == nil; tx.Commit(); assert stored T1.expires_at == later and every other member is as before; advance the clock 2h; assert GET /api/v1/user/tokens with T1 is 200; advance the clock to later; assert it is 401; then earlier: SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, T2.id, clock.now - 1s), commit; assert a request with T2 is 401; SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, T4.id, later), commit; assert T4.revoked_at is unchanged and a request with T4 is 401; err = identity.SetTokenExpiryByID(tx, 'zzzzzzzz', later); assert errors.Is(err, the not-found error of internal/identity); assert no row changed and no event was written

requirements.title: Changing a PAT's permissions
requirements.rationale: A token's reach can be adjusted without issuing a new value, but never beyond what the adjusting credential holds.

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:write or tokens:manage) sends PUT /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with a non-empty array of registered scopes for a live PAT of its own user
criteria.action: replace the token's permissions with the list given, duplicates dropped and order kept
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token after the change; the token is scope-checked against the new list from the next request on

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live PAT T with [git:read, changes:write]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = PUT /api/v1/user/tokens/<T>/permissions {permissions:['vars:read','git:write','vars:read']} as alice's API key; assert r.status == 200; assert r.permissions == ['vars:read','git:write']; assert r.revoked_at == null; assert GET /user/tokens/<T>.permissions is the same; assert a request with T's value on a stub route needing changes:read now gets 403 insufficient_scope

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:write or tokens:manage) sends PATCH /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with a non-empty array of registered scopes for a live PAT of its own user
criteria.action: append the given scopes the token does not yet have, in the order given, after the existing ones and keep the scopes already present as they are
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token after the change

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live PAT T with [git:read, changes:write]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = PATCH /api/v1/user/tokens/<T>/permissions {permissions:['changes:write','vars:read','vars:read']}; assert r.status == 200; assert r.permissions == ['git:read','changes:write','vars:read']

criteria.condition: a user credential (an API key, or a PAT holding tokens:write or tokens:manage) sends DELETE /user/tokens/:token_id/permissions with a non-empty array of strings for a live PAT of its own user
criteria.action: remove the given scopes from the token's permissions, ignore every given string the token does not have whether registered or not, and apply no subset rule
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token after the change

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live PAT T with [git:read, changes:write, vars:read]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go: r = DELETE /api/v1/user/tokens/<T>/permissions {permissions:['changes:write','git:write','not-a-scope']} as alice's PAT holding only [tokens:write]; assert r.status == 200; assert r.permissions == ['git:read','vars:read']; assert r.revoked_at == null

criteria.condition: a PUT with an empty permissions array, or a DELETE on the permissions route, leaves a live PAT with no scope
criteria.action: store the empty permissions list and revoke the token in the same transaction
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Token, permissions [] and revoked_at set; the token no longer authenticates

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over changes on a live PAT with [git:read, vars:read]: {PUT permissions []}, {DELETE permissions ['git:read','vars:read']}, {DELETE ['vars:read'] then DELETE ['git:read']}: assert last r.status == 200; assert r.permissions == []; assert r.revoked_at == clock.now; assert a request with the token's value -> 401

criteria.condition: the body of a permissions route has no permissions member or one that is not an array of strings, or a PUT or PATCH body names a string that is not a registered scope, or a PATCH or DELETE body has an empty permissions array
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the token unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 400 with error_type invalid_request; the token's permissions and revoked_at are unchanged

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
alice's live PAT T with [git:read]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over (method, body): {PUT, {}}, {PUT, {permissions:'git:read'}}, {PUT, {permissions:['git:admin']}}, {PUT, {permissions:[5]}}, {PATCH, {}}, {PATCH, {permissions:[]}}, {PATCH, {permissions:['git:read','nope']}}, {DELETE, {}}, {DELETE, {permissions:[]}}, {DELETE, {permissions:'git:read'}}: assert r.status == 400; assert r.error.error_type == 'invalid_request'; assert GET /user/tokens/<T>.permissions is unchanged

criteria.condition: a PAT sends a PUT or PATCH on a permissions route that would add to the target token a scope the calling PAT does not itself hold, counting no implication
criteria.action: refuse the request, name the first such scope and leave the token unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 403 with error_type insufficient_scope and a message containing the first offending scope; the target token is unchanged

alice has the PATs C and T

criteria.condition: a valid PUT, PATCH or DELETE on a permissions route names a PAT of the caller's user that is revoked or expired
criteria.action: refuse the request and leave the token unchanged
criteria.contract: HTTP 409 with error_type conflict; the token is unchanged

alice has a revoked PAT and an expired PAT, each with [git:read]
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/token_routes_test.go, a table over methods {PUT, PATCH, DELETE} and targets {revoked PAT, expired PAT} with body {permissions:['git:read']}: as alice's API key assert r.status == 409; assert r.error.error_type == 'conflict'; assert the stored token is unchanged

criteria.action: for any permission change, leave the token's paths, workspace, name and expires_at as they were and ignore body members named paths and workspace
criteria.contract: the Token in the response and in later reads carries the paths, workspace, name and expires_at it was created with

requirements.title: Admin key and token routes
requirements.rationale: An operator must be able to see and cut off any user's credentials without that user's cooperation.

criteria.condition: an admin (the admin token, or an API key whose user has role admin) sends GET /users/:id/keys with a selector of an existing user
criteria.action: answer with every API key of the selected user in any state, newest first
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: Key[], next_cursor}

setup: a hub started in-process with a temporary store; user alice with a live API key; a fixed test clock
an admin-role user root with an API key; the hub's admin token; alice has a live and a revoked key and three PATs (live, revoked, expired)
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/admin_credential_routes_test.go, a table over callers {the admin token, the API key of admin-role user root} and selectors {alice's UUID, 'alice@example.com', 'alice'}: r = GET /api/v1/users/<sel>/keys; assert r.status == 200; assert ids(r.items) == alice's keys newest first, the revoked one included; assert no item carries a secret

criteria.condition: an admin sends GET /users/:id/tokens with a selector of an existing user
criteria.action: answer with every PAT of the selected user in any state, tokens with a workspace binding included, newest first
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with {items: Token[], next_cursor}

criteria.condition: an admin sends DELETE /users/:id/keys/:key_id or DELETE /users/:id/tokens/:token_id naming a key or token of the selected user
criteria.action: set revoked_at of that key or token to the present instant when it is not yet revoked, and change nothing when it already is
criteria.contract: HTTP 200 with the Key or Token, revoked_at set; a repeated call answers 200 with the same revoked_at; the credential no longer authenticates

setup: the fixture of the admin key list test
check.pseudocode: in internal/identity/admin_credential_routes_test.go, a table over (route, target): {DELETE /users/alice/keys/<live key>}, {DELETE /users/alice/tokens/<live token>}, {DELETE /users/alice/tokens/<expired token>}: first = send as the admin token; assert first.status == 200; assert first.revoked_at == clock.now; assert the credential's value -> 401 on GET /api/v1/user; advance the clock one hour; second = send as root's API key; assert second.status == 200 and second.revoked_at == first.revoked_at

criteria.condition: GET /users/:id/keys, GET /users/:id/tokens, DELETE /users/:id/keys/:key_id or DELETE /users/:id/tokens/:token_id is called with an API key whose user has role user, or with any PAT
criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing

criteria.action: refuse the request and change nothing
criteria.contract: HTTP 404 with error_type not_found; no key or token is changed

requirements.title: CLI commands for API keys
requirements.rationale: A developer rotates and revokes the key on their machine without editing the config file by hand.

criteria.condition: the developer runs parley keys list
criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/user/keys with the configured credential and print the response body on stdout
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds the list document

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/keys_test.go: run(['keys','list']); assert the stub saw GET /api/v1/user/keys with Authorization: Bearer <configured key>; assert stdout is the canned list as JSON indented by 2 spaces; assert exit == 0

criteria.condition: the developer runs parley keys refresh with an API key configured
criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/user/keys/<key_id>/refresh with the key_id taken from the configured API key, print the response on stdout, warn on stderr that the key will not be shown again, then replace api_key in the config file with the new key, keeping the file's other keys and mode 0600
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds {key, key_id, expires_at}; the config file holds the new key

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
the config file also holds an unknown key extra = 'x'
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/keys_test.go: config api_key = 'parley_Ab3dE6gH_<32 chars>'; stub answers 200 {key:'parley_Ab3dE6gH_<new>', key_id:'Ab3dE6gH', expires_at:...}; run(['keys','refresh']); assert the stub saw POST /api/v1/user/keys/Ab3dE6gH/refresh; assert stdout == the response; assert stderr mentions that the key is not shown again; assert config.toml api_key == the new key, endpoint_url, user_id and an unknown key 'extra' are preserved, and the file mode is 0600; assert exit == 0

criteria.condition: the developer runs parley keys refresh or parley keys revoke and the configured credential is not an API key (a PAT, the admin token or a value of no known format)
criteria.action: fail before sending any request
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stderr holds an error envelope with error_type client_error; nothing on stdout; no request is sent

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/keys_test.go, a table over commands {keys refresh, keys revoke} and credentials {'parley_pat_k3x9q2mz_<32 chars>', 'parley_admin_<64 hex>', 'garbage'}: run; assert exit == 2; assert stderr is the error envelope with code 0 and error_type 'client_error'; assert stdout == ''; assert the stub saw no request; assert config.toml is unchanged

criteria.condition: parley keys refresh received the new key from the hub and the config file cannot be written or does not exist
criteria.action: still print the response with the new key on stdout, warn on stderr that the new key was not saved, and exit with a client error
criteria.contract: exit code 2; stdout holds the complete response including the new key; stderr holds the warning

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/keys_test.go, a table: {config directory made read-only after loading}, {no config file, credential and endpoint given by PARLEY_API_KEY and PARLEY_ENDPOINT_URL}: stub answers 200 with a new key; run(['keys','refresh']); assert stdout == the response including key; assert stderr mentions that the key was not saved; assert exit == 2; in the second row assert no config.toml was created

criteria.condition: the developer runs parley keys revoke with an API key configured
criteria.action: send DELETE /api/v1/user/keys/<key_id> for the configured API key, print the response on stdout, clear api_key and user_id in the config file, and tell the user on stderr to run parley login
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds the revoked Key; the config file no longer holds the credential; when the hub answers an error the config file is unchanged and the exit code is 1

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/keys_test.go: stub answers 200 with a Key whose revoked_at is set; run(['keys','revoke']); assert the stub saw DELETE /api/v1/user/keys/Ab3dE6gH; assert stdout == the Key; assert config.toml has no non-empty api_key or user_id and still has endpoint_url; assert 'parley login' in stderr; assert exit == 0; row with no config file and the credential from PARLEY_API_KEY: exit == 0 and no file is created; row where the stub answers 404: exit == 1, stderr is the hub's envelope, config.toml unchanged

criteria.condition: the operator runs parley admin keys list <user> or parley admin keys revoke <user> <key_id>
criteria.action: send GET /api/v1/users/<user>/keys for list, or DELETE /api/v1/users/<user>/keys/<key_id> for revoke, with each argument percent-encoded as one path segment, and print the response body on stdout
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds the list or the revoked Key; a wrong argument count is exit code 2 with error_type usage_error and no request

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/admin_keys_test.go: run(['admin','keys','list','alice']); assert the stub saw GET /api/v1/users/alice/keys; assert stdout == canned list; run(['admin','keys','list','a/b']); assert the request's escaped path is /api/v1/users/a%2Fb/keys; run(['admin','keys','revoke','alice','Ab3dE6gH']); assert the stub saw DELETE /api/v1/users/alice/keys/Ab3dE6gH; assert exit == 0 for both; table of wrong argument counts {admin keys list, admin keys revoke alice}: exit == 2, error_type 'usage_error', no request

requirements.title: CLI commands for PATs
requirements.rationale: Minting and adjusting tokens is what a developer does most often before handing work to an agent.

criteria.condition: the developer runs parley tokens create with --name and --permissions
criteria.action: send POST /api/v1/user/tokens with name, permissions split at commas, paths (present only when --paths was given: every --paths value split at commas, in order) and expires (90 when the flag is absent), print the response on stdout and warn on stderr that the token value will not be shown again
criteria.contract: exit code 0; stdout holds the Token with its token member; stderr holds the warning

setup: a stub hub (net/http/httptest) that records requests and answers canned bodies; PARLEY_CONFIG_DIR set to t.TempDir() with a config.toml holding endpoint_url, api_key and user_id
check.pseudocode: in internal/cli/tokens_test.go: run(['tokens','create','--name','ci','--permissions','git:read,changes:write','--paths','docs/**,src/*.go','--paths','README.md','--expires','30']); assert the stub saw POST /api/v1/user/tokens with JSON body {name:'ci', permissions:['git:read','changes:write'], paths:['docs/**','src/*.go','README.md'], expires:30} and Content-Type application/json; assert stdout == the canned Token including token; assert stderr mentions that the value is not shown again; assert exit == 0; row without --paths and --expires: the body has no paths member and expires == 90

criteria.condition: a parley tokens command is run without a required flag (--name or --permissions on create, --permissions on replace, add and remove), with a wrong number of arguments, or with an --expires that is not an integer
criteria.action: fail before sending any request

execution_paths.title: A developer mints a path-scoped token, an agent narrows it, and the developer revokes it

steps.action: runs parley tokens create --name ci --permissions git:read,tokens:manage --paths 'docs/**'
sends POST /api/v1/user/tokens with the developer's API key
validates the body, stores the token with a hash of its secret and answers 201 with the token value
prints the Token with its value on stdout and warns on stderr that the value is not shown again
sends POST /api/v1/user/tokens with that token, asking for git:write
applies the subset rule and answers 403 insufficient_scope naming git:write
sends POST /api/v1/user/tokens asking for git:read with paths ['docs/api/*.md']
finds the permission held and the glob covered and answers 201 with a second token
runs parley tokens revoke with the first token's id
sets revoked_at on the first token and answers 200; the agent's next request with it is answered 401

real_components: parleyd HTTP server with authentication, scope check and token routes
setup: a parleyd started in-process on 127.0.0.1:0 with a temporary data directory, as the tests of test/e2e start it
a user alice with a live API key, and a CLI config directory pointing at the hub with that key
end_state: parley tokens list shows two tokens of alice: the first with revoked_at set and paths ['docs/**'], the second live with permissions ['git:read'] and paths ['docs/api/*.md']
GET /api/v1/user/tokens with the first token's value answers 401
the refused request created no token
smoke.pseudocode: in test/e2e/tokens_test.go: out = cli('tokens','create','--name','ci','--permissions','git:read,tokens:manage','--paths','docs/**'); t1 = out.json; assert http(POST /api/v1/user/tokens, bearer t1.token, {name:'w', permissions:['git:write']}).status == 403; r2 = http(POST /api/v1/user/tokens, bearer t1.token, {name:'n', permissions:['git:read'], paths:['docs/api/*.md']}); assert r2.status == 201; cli('tokens','revoke', t1.token_id); assert http(GET /api/v1/user/tokens, bearer t1.token).status == 401; list = cli('tokens','list').json.items; assert len(list) == 2 and the item t1.token_id has revoked_at != null

execution_paths.title: A developer refreshes the API key on their machine

steps.action: runs parley keys refresh
reads key_id from the configured API key and sends POST /api/v1/user/keys/<key_id>/refresh
replaces the key's secret, restarts its lifetime and answers 200 with the new key
prints the response and saves the new key to the config file
runs parley keys list
authenticates the new key and answers the list, which holds the same key_id

sends DELETE /api/v1/users/alice/tokens/<token_id>
